framing: r3 flip list applied, AND conditioned on C-GAB — the first parameter-side lever of the gauntlet
hypothesis: Round 3 went BACKWARDS on the axis it tried to fix: object-not-surface culls rose 3 to 6, and the specific failures were doorways, braziers, hearths, arches and hatches. The 'fragment of a long wall with no centre' framing did not read as 'no landmark' — it read as 'a wall, and therefore a wall WITH SOMETHING IN IT'. Asking a single-object generator for a wall keeps returning the most object-like wall available. Three text framings have now failed in three different ways: object (r1 Stage-1 shape), noise (micro-probe), landmark (r3). This round keeps applying the flip list but adds the one lever that is not text at all — style conditioning on C-GAB, which the STOP 1 smoke test measured as propagating material DNA in 12 of 12 and which Rafe named as the compositionally neutral parent (VAB is charactered stock, not a style parent). If conditioning fixes the palette drift and the material at once, that is worth more than any further wording. Round 5 runs this same prompt BARE so the conditioning is attributable.
description: A dungeon wall of cold grey quarried stone, seen straight on from the front. Level courses of blocks, the courses uneven in height and the vertical joints offset irregularly, blocks of different lengths, three or four of them replaced with mismatched salvage stone. The mortar joints are much darker than the block faces, roughly a third of their brightness, and each block carries a single lighter pixel along its top edge. Where a block has been replaced the gap around it is packed with smaller chipped stone in a coarser, paler mortar, so the eye reads old block, new packing, old block. Laid horizontally across the whole width is a squared timber baulk that runs off both the left and right edges and continues past them, standing proud of the stone with a darker under-edge. It is fixed by two driven iron pins, each a small square head with a bitten rim, and the stone around each is bruised dark. One turn of rope is wrapped over the timber where it crosses a joint. The top four rows of the frame are the wall's upper surface: one flat value, clearly lighter than the front face, meeting it on a single hard line. Everything below that is front face, all the way to the bottom of the frame. Stone from edge to edge.

parameter_provenance.note: ⚠ TWO THINGS CHANGE THIS ROUND — the flip list AND conditioning — which normally makes a result unattributable. It is done knowingly and the attribution is bought back by design: round 5 runs THIS EXACT PROMPT bare, so the conditioned/bare pair isolates the lever.
